knownStaleness.topic: Population shares and religious affiliation in Who We Are
knownStaleness.problem: The chapter's proportions are from the 2006 census era and the 2021 Census has moved all of them. The guide says First Nations are "about 65%" of Indigenous people (2021: 58.0%), that "about half" of First Nations people live on reserve (2021: 40.6% among status First Nations), and that "the great majority of Canadians identify as Christians" (2021: 53.3%, just over half). The last is the worst for a learning game: "No religion" is now 34.6%, larger than Catholic at 29.9%, so a question teaching the guide's framing punishes a learner who knows the current figure. Recorded at chapter grain for a few minutes on 2026-09-08, which forced volatile on all 46 questions in the chapter when three carry the shares — the same defect this register already had for the Oath, repeated by the same hand within the hour.
knownStaleness.action: volatile: never put one of these shares in an option or an explanation. The live page (who-are-canadians.html, Date modified 2025-08-08) still carries every one of them, so the modification date is not evidence of revision and re-fetching resolves nothing. Recorded here as prose first, which was the same defect ADR-0016 section 1 had already fixed: that sentence is a live check, and it has been transcribed into liveChecks[] where a gate can read it and where it expires. With it, Who We Are is on ADR-0016 section 2 row 2, so the volatile demand no longer fires on the fifteen questions that share pages 17, 18 and 21 with these shares and carry facts that will never move - treaty rights, the Royal Proclamation, residential schools, the 2008 apology, the meaning of "Inuit", Michif. bannedFromAnswers is the whole mitigation on row 2, and the clock that keeps it honest is liveChecks[].checkedAt, not a per-question re-fetch. Claim-level grain would still be finer than page grain, but it is no longer what this entry costs: page grain now over-reaches only into a term search, not into fifteen re-verifications.

knownStaleness.topic: The G8 and Russia's membership in Canada's Economy
knownStaleness.problem: Page 90 lists Russia among the G8. Russia was suspended in March 2014 and the group has met as the G7 ever since. Confirmed against the live page on 2026-09-09, Date modified 2025-04-11: it still names Russia, eleven years on.
knownStaleness.action: G7 is banned beside G8 deliberately: an option naming the G7 is right about the world and wrong about the document the exam is drawn from, so no answer may rest on the group's name in either direction. The flag stops at the G8 clause -- the same sentence's ranking claim is volatile's job, and folding it in would over-fire onto a usable proposition and repeat the grain defect this register keeps closing.

knownStaleness.topic: The English lyrics of O Canada
knownStaleness.problem: Page 84 prints "True patriot love in all thy sons command". Bill C-210 received royal assent on 2018-02-07 and replaced that line with "in all of us command". Confirmed against the live page on 2026-09-09, Date modified 2026-05-14 -- four months old -- still printing the pre-2018 line.
knownStaleness.action: Both the stale line and the current one are banned, for the reason G7 is banned beside G8. The two facts flanking it on the same page -- proclaimed 1980, first sung in Quebec City 1880 -- cannot move and are what the shipped questions grade.

knownStaleness.topic: NAFTA and its replacement in Canada's Economy
knownStaleness.problem: Page 90 says Mexico joined in 1994 in "the broader North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA)". NAFTA was replaced by CUSMA on 2020-07-01. The live page, Date modified 2025-04-11, still says NAFTA, so this is upstream and permanent -- the same disposition as the G8 entry beside it.
knownStaleness.action: Both the dead name and the current one are banned, for the reason G7 is banned beside G8: an option naming CUSMA is right about the world and wrong about the document the exam is drawn from. The two shipped questions on this sentence survive it, because they grade the year and the country rather than the agreement's name. Recorded and not flagged: the same sentence's "over 444 million people and over $1 trillion in merchandise trade in 2008" is a 2008 figure printed as current. Nothing cites it and nothing should.

knownStaleness.topic: The 2008 trade and population figures in Canada's Economy
knownStaleness.problem: Page 90 prints "over 444 million people and over $1 trillion in merchandise trade in 2008" as a present-tense description of North American free trade. It is an eighteen-year-old magnitude in the same sentence as NAFTA, which was replaced by CUSMA on 2020-07-01, so the sentence is stale twice over for two different reasons. Confirmed against the live page (canadas-economy.html, Date modified 2025-04-11) on 2026-09-09: it still prints the same 2008 figures. Nothing in the bank cites them today. ADR-0028 sends an author onto this page's neighbours looking for propositions, and a number in a sentence is the most quotable thing on a short page, so this is recorded before it is needed rather than after.
knownStaleness.action: No option or explanation may rest on a trade volume or a population total from this page, and that includes a corrected one: a 2026 figure is right about the world and wrong about the document the exam is drawn from, which is the reason G7 is banned beside G8 in the entry above. The teachable propositions in this sentence are the DATES and the PARTNERS -- free trade with the United States in 1988, Mexico joining in 1994 -- and both are already claimed. Ask about those or about nothing here.

knownStaleness.problem: Every population count in the chapter is a 2011-era figure printed in the present tense. Page 94: "Canada has a population of about 34 million people" (2021 Census 36,991,981, and past 41 million since). Page 98: "Nearly eight million people live in Quebec". Page 99: "At more than 12 million, the people of Ontario". Page 102: British Columbia "with a population of four million". Page 103: the three territories "have a population of only 100,000". Page 104: Yellowknife "(population 20,000)" and, on page 100, St. Boniface's Francophone community "at 45,000". Confirmed against the live page (canadas-regions.html, Date modified 2025-05-12) on 2026-09-10: every figure is still there, unchanged.
knownStaleness.action: No option and no explanation may state a population from this chapter, and that includes a CORRECTED one - a 2026 count is right about the world and wrong about the document the exam is drawn from, which is the reason G7 is banned beside G8 on page 90. The terms above are the literal spellings the guide uses; the rule is wider than the list and a figure written with a non-breaking space or spelled out ("thirty-four million") evades the matcher without evading the rule. What the chapter offers instead, and what the fourteen shipped economy questions grade, is which province produces WHAT - resources, industries, ports and capitals - none of which is a magnitude.

knownStaleness.topic: Shares, proportions and rankings in Canada's Regions
knownStaleness.problem: The chapter's proportions are census-era or output-share figures that have moved, and its rankings are point-in-time. Page 94: Ottawa is "Canada's fourth largest metropolitan area". Page 98: Quebec's "More than three-quarters speak French as their first language" (2021 Census 74.8% mother tongue, now under three-quarters) and "Ontario and Quebec produce more than three-quarters of all Canadian manufactured goods". Page 99: Ontario is "more than one-third of Canadians". Page 100: Manitoba's "14% reporting Ukrainian origins" and "largest Aboriginal population of any province, at over 15%" (2021: 18.1%, and largest by SHARE only - Ontario is largest by count), and Saskatchewan's "40% of the arable land in Canada". Page 102: "About one-half of all the goods produced in B.C. are forestry products" and "approximately 600 provincial parks". Confirmed against the live page on 2026-09-10: all still present, unchanged.
knownStaleness.action: Ask which province produces a thing, never what share of it. "Ontario and Quebec make most of Canada's manufactured goods" is durable and is what eco-25 grades; "more than three-quarters" is not, and sits in that question's source.quote only, where nothing a player reads can inherit it. Two entries here are deliberately narrower than the stale fact and this says so rather than letting the list imply coverage: "one-third" is NOT banned, because the territories holding one-third of Canada's land mass is geography and cannot move, and Ontario at more than one-third of Canadians is still true; and bare "half" and "moitié" are not banned because they are ordinary words whose every use would fire. A share that slips through in those spellings is caught by the verifier reading the chapter, not here.

knownStaleness.topic: The pre-accession monarch in Canada's Regions
knownStaleness.problem: Page 94 dates Ottawa's selection as capital to "1857 by Queen Victoria, the great-great-grandmother of Queen Elizabeth II". The reigning monarch is King Charles III, so the relationship the sentence states is one generation short and the title is wrong. Recorded separately from "The monarch and the Governor General", which covers page 57 in two other chapters, because this is a different sentence on a different page and ADR-0016's register is one entry per claim - the same reason G8 and NAFTA are separate entries on page 90. Confirmed against the live page on 2026-09-10: unchanged. Note that page 104's "Queen Elizabeth I in 1576" is a sixteenth-century reference and is correct; the banned term is "Elizabeth II" and does not reach it.
knownStaleness.action: Route the answers around the Sovereign entirely on this page. The durable proposition in the sentence is that Ottawa was chosen as the capital in 1857, and it can be asked without naming any monarch. No economy question cites page 94; this flag is recorded before it is needed, for the regions bank that ADR-0028 sends to these same pages.

knownStaleness.topic: The size of Nunavut's Legislative Assembly
knownStaleness.problem: Page 104 says "The 19-member Legislative Assembly chooses a premier and ministers by consensus." Nunavut's Legislative Assembly has had 22 seats since the 2013 general election. The consensus government mechanism the sentence describes is correct and durable; only the count is wrong. Confirmed against the live page on 2026-09-10: still 19.
knownStaleness.action: Both the stale count and the current one are banned, for the reason G7 is banned beside G8: an option saying 22 is right about Nunavut and wrong about the document the exam is drawn from. Ask about consensus government, which is the teachable and unmoving part of the sentence. Recorded at page grain on 104 alone; no shipped question cites that page.

liveChecks.consequence: IRCC has not revised Discover Canada for the accession. The live pages still read "Her Majesty is a symbol of Canadian sovereignty", "53 other nations", "Her Majesty's Loyal Opposition" and "308 electoral districts", and caption a photo "Queen Elizabeth II". So our cache is not drifting behind a maintained source: the source itself is unrevised, cache and live agree, and both are out of date. A drift-based quarantine has no trigger and re-fetching cannot resolve a stale fact. What makes the bank shippable is bannedFromAnswers, not a future fetch.

liveChecks.consequence: Fetched first-hand, twice, in answer to ADR-0028's precondition that this chapter be live-checked before any economy question cites it. Fourteen economy questions (eco-20 to eco-33) now do. The live page agrees with the cached extraction on every one of the twenty-two claims above, including every point-in-time figure: the 2011-era population totals, the census-era shares, the pre-accession "great-great-grandmother of Queen Elizabeth II" on page 94 and Nunavut's 19-member Legislative Assembly, which has had 22 seats since 2013. The Date modified of 2025-05-12 is therefore not evidence of revision, exactly as it was not for Who We Are: the page has been touched and these facts have not. Disposition is does-not-revise and the mitigation is the four page-grain flags added beside this entry, not a future fetch. What was NOT found is worth recording because ADR-0028 predicted it: the chapter does not call Nunavut "Canada's newest territory" anywhere, so that anticipated flag has no referent. All fourteen new questions were checked against every banned term these flags introduce and none contains a digit or a fraction in any option or explanation, in either language. This entry puts Canada's Regions on ADR-0016 section 2 row 2, so the flags demand no volatile marking, and the clock that keeps them honest is this checkedAt - 2027-03-09.
